summary:
February 15, 1973 


I just now received the Sladek parody, and it is the real me. It truly is. Read­ ing it was one of the great moments of my life; I mean it. I kept saying to Tessa, my girlfriend, who was sitting beside me trying to read her junk mail, “Hey, this is better than I do! Much better! But still me!” “Then why are you laughing?” Tessa says, eying me uneasily. “It shows how really great a writer I am!” That really is my feeling about it, Ed. The guy whose stuff is being parodied has to be good to produce such a great work as Sladek has done, here; if I’d never read my own stuff or even heard of me, I’d go out looking for it after reading his parody. 

At least I hopemy writing is the expression of talent; Sladek’s parody (as well as other pieces of his I’ve read) the expression of genius. In a sense, his parody is the best thing I’ve ever written or probably ever will write, except as regards all the genuinely brilliant touches, he did it. It’s amazing to find the entire body of your own life’s work the premise for something better. Wow. 

Oddly, my story for FINAL STAGE is somewhat influenced by Sladek. I do find him an impressive writer, one from whom I can—and have—learned much already. An odd coincidence, in view of his parody, which I hadn’t yet read ...
